item.title: SCP-5278:
item.content:encoded:
This is a slightly confusing article to read. When did the mine shut down? When did everyone die? How old is this guys daughter? It feels like they were supposed to have died over a hundred years ago or something but the way this all sounds it was very recent. It doesn't convey anything very well.

It doesn't feel very well thought out, it could use some more work, its not bad just needs more to it besides a conversation between two characters and a small amount of technical talk. -1

Edit: i also wanted to ask, why is this scp restricted to level 3 staff? And why does it need an mtf?

item.title: SCP-5965:
item.content:encoded:
As someone who lost a close family member in a traumatic way, this hits home. Some may think the final log is too on the nose but I find it incredibly haunting… I lived this person’s pain, and Dysadron perfectly captures the feelings of loss and permanence that so haunted me for years after my mother died.

It’s a hell of an article

item.title: SCP-5016:
item.content:encoded:
Necroing, but i have to say. I had to downvote in the end. I wanted to enjoy this, it started out okay. The hook got me interested, at first. a tower underground with seemingly endless floors that have a puzzle? Cool, let me hear about it.

But, as other have pointed out this gets a bit self-indulgent. The strengths fade fast as you read; theres a lot of errors that have existed since you posted this article originally. And while i understand translating is no simple task, you said you were going to have someone look over it for you. Doesnt appear that way.

Beyond the grammar errors, its just too unbelievable. 343? Why mention 038-FR? Theres too much going on. So, like i said -1.

item.title: SCP-2719:
item.content:encoded:
In the last batch of tests, several O5 try to undergo transcendence by making Transcendence become Charles, then Injecting themselves into it. That said, -1, -2 and -3 become inside rather than go inside. From that, I believe that when Inject failed due to -1, -2 and -3 being wholly unable to "transcend" for whatever reason, Point was cast instead. Therefore, here are my hypotheses:
If the target of Inject is an abstract concept while Charles is a physical concept, target is outside.
If the target of Inject cannot conform in any conceptual or physical way to being "inside" Charles, Point is cast on the target instead.

My last hypothesis was initially "If Point is cast on Charles, Charles is outside", but while it would conform to the logs, it would make no logical sense. Following previous nomenclature, casting Point on Charles should rather return "Is inside" or "Was inside".
Therefore, here is my last hypothesis :
Some concepts, such as "SCP-682" and "Transcendence", are currently outside and cannot become inside.

item.title: SCP-2010: Not as Anglo-dependent as you'd suppose
item.content:encoded: The languages of Sweden, Denmark, and Norway all use vowel #3 as a one-letter preposed term — used very commonly to express subject enclosure, and therefore necessary for SCP records. Furthermore, Denmark's language also uses vowel #3 as a second-person plural pronoun — so that the Northern branch would not have an easy job when two or more personnel put mother-tongue research talks on paper. (My own name would get the black box, as that name has vowel #3 at the start!)

item.title: SCP-5057 Additional Documentation:
item.content:encoded:
So I don’t comment often, but when you wrote the original skip for this, I left a grumbly comment about how it broke my heart and gave you an upvote.

But I don’t know if it’s stress about the state of the world in world in general right now or what, but you had me crying happy tears. This is my new comfort skip. The way this all tied together was perfect. The choice to make this an additional file rather than add to the original was perfect, as you still get that guy punch feeling at the end of the original.

Thanks for being a psychic and posting this on a day where the world, or at least my country, needed a touch of brightness. +1
